newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron violence rages on over pig posters.
newsitem.headline: Hebron violence rages on over pig posters.

text.p: Israeli troops firing rubber bullets wounded at least 25 Palestinians in the volatile West Bank town of Hebron on Friday after coming under a hail of bricks, bombs and bottles, witnesses and hospital sources said.
A Palestinian boy was rushed to Hebron's al-Ahli hospital after a rubber-coated metal pellet fired by Israeli troops penetrated his skull. Hospital sources said the boy was in stable condition.

Friday's clashes, which subsided towards evening, erupted after dozens of Palestinian demonstrators jeered street activists from Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's Fatah faction who tried to intervene to dampen renewed violence.

"Allahu Akbar! (God is Greatest)," demonstrators shouted as they hurled stones, bottles and petrol bombs at battle-ready Israeli troops on the confrontation line between Israeli- and Palestinian-run sectors of Hebron.
The forces responded with a barrage of rubber bullets.

The city's heart has been a battleground since a Jewish woman ignited Arab anger last week by pasting anti-Moslem placards depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig stamping on the Koran with one hoof and writing in it with another.

In PLO-ruled Gaza, 14-year-old Palestinian deaf mute Ibrahim Abu Rteimeh, who was in a coma since being shot near a Jewish settlement last month, died of his wounds, al-Shifa hospital sources said. Palestinians said an Israeli soldier shot him.
In the West Bank town of Nablus, about 5,000 Palestinians marched in protest against the pig posters in a demonstration organised by the militant Islamist group Hamas, witnesses said.
The protesters burned the U.S. and Israeli flags and an effigy of a Jewish settler, depicted wearing a skullcap and beard.
To avoid trouble, the Israeli army barred Jewish worshippers from reaching Joseph's Tomb, an Israeli-run Jewish shrine within the PLO-ruled town.
A 26-year-old Jewish woman was charged on Thursday with illegally posting the anti-Moslem placards in Hebron.
Witnesses said a home-made bomb exploded in Hebron's casbah in the same alley where a similar device wounded two Israeli soldiers earlier in the week.
"Whoever throws a bomb with the intention of killing someone will also meet his death," Israeli West Bank Commander Major-General Gabi Ofir told army radio.
Israel sealed Hebron on Friday to try to stifle unrest, bracing for violence following weekly Moslem Friday prayers.
"Since the morning, the Israeli army is preventing the entrance of Palestinians who do not live in Hebron to the (Palestinian-ruled) H1 area for security reasons," an army statement said.

Palestinians have demanded that Israel remove the 400 Jewish settlers who remained in fortified enclaves in the heart of the city of 100,000 Arabs since Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO self-rule in January.
"I want to make one thing clear: We will continue to live here and we will continue to build," Hebron Jewish settler Moshe Ben Zimra told army radio.
